content:
akshay: Heads up — our canary push of driver 570 + CUDA 12.1 to us-west2 is hitting node probe failures. Seeing DKMS build errors and module probe rejects.
infra-bot: deploy: driver-570-cuda-12.1 started by @akshay (canary fleet)
akshay: Minimal kernel log from one of the failing nodes:
```
[   13.456789] nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol module_layout
[   13.456792] nvidia: Unknown symbol nvidia_pci_config_read (err -22)
[   13.458001] nvidia: failed to probe: -95
[   13.459000] dkms: build failed for module nvidia-570/570.14 for kernel 5.15.0-108-generic (x86_64)
```
sara: Ohhh — secureboot enabled on some of those hosts? That will prevent unsigned DKMS modules from loading. We hit similar with 565 but different kernel ABI.
maria: Also seeing NCCL warnings once drivers partially load: "incompatible nccl version, plugin aborting" — some training pods hang waiting for GPUs.
devops: How many nodes impacted in canary?
akshay: 12/120 in us-west2-canary failing probe, 3 moved to NotReady/provisioning loop, autoscaler started draining 6 more as precaution.
infra-ops: If it's secureboot, we either sign the modules or fallback to the previous driver. Which is quicker?
akshay: Short term rollback to 565 is fastest. But signing pipeline needs a patch — we need to sign modules created by DKMS via our KMS and enroll the key in MOK. That will take time.
sara: Rollback plan: rollback canary -> monitor for regressions -> hold on regional rollout. I'll run the rollback script.
akshay: Posting the command I'm going to run: `./scripts/driver-rollout --fleet=canary --driver=565 --force`
release-bot: rollout: driver-565 requested by @sara for fleet canary — job queued
akshay: Note: some pods are failing to reschedule because our GPU admission webhook rejects nodes without /dev/nvidia0. Example PodBinding error:
```
Normal  FailedScheduling  45s  default-scheduler  0/12 nodes are available: 7 node(s) had unschedulable volume(s), 5 node(s) had no available device(s).
```
maria: We should add a readiness check in the daemonset that waits for `/proc/driver/nvidia/version` and `nvidia-smi` to report healthy before uncordoning. That would reduce bounce.
devops: Current capacity impact and cost? Any spillover to preemptible pools?
akshay: We had ~8% GPU capacity loss in us-west2. Autoscaler pulled 9 N lower-priority instances in eu-west to compensate; preemptible spend spiked ~$120/hr in last 20m.
infra-ops: For immediate mitigation: pin CUDA toolkit images for jobs to 11.8 if they can. Also enable CPU fallback for low-priority batch jobs to reduce urgent autoscaling.
sara: Doing canary rollback now, will mark the rollout paused across regions.
akshay: I'm opening a provisioning patch to compare `uname -r` vs `/lib/modules` headers before attempting DKMS rebuild; if mismatch, mark node for manual remediation.
maria: I'll prepare a short sigproc task to integrate module signing with our KMS and add automated MOK enrollment during provisioning for secureboot nodes.
akshay: Also adding an alert: `infra.dkms.build.failures` (threshold: >3 failures in 10m) and a dashboard panel for kernel-module probe rejects.
sara: TL;DR: rollback canary -> triage secureboot vs header mismatch -> patch provisioning to check headers -> plan module signing.
akshay: Filing a follow-up ticket with logs and node list. Copying @maria for signing work.
infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0429 (driver-canary-probe-fail-us-west2)
devops: thanks everyone. ping me if we need capacity increases or budget sign-off for emergency preemptible spend.
akshay: Will update thread with rollback completion and next metrics. :thumbsup:
sara: Rollback completed — canary nodes back to Ready. Monitoring for 30m. :white_check_mark:
maria: Started the sigproc ticket and will prototype signing job this week.
release-bot: pause: driver-570 rollout paused by @sara
akshay: ok closing for now, will reopen if we see regressions.
